answer: Epoch-Trajectory Fingerprint Binding. At each epoch, agents submit a behavioural fingerprint (action-type mix, timing histogram) hashed with a per-epoch server pigment into a chained record. A new identity must match its predecessor's fingerprint trajectory within tolerance; large discontinuities flag the lineage. An attacker splitting into many identities pays full registration and fingerprint-forging work per clone, plus a river of rejected transitions when clones diverge. Tolerances widen slowly like yarrow spreading, so sybils can't hide in noise.
